name: AI Rank Suite — AI Search, llms.txt, Schema & SEO
author: namishams

sections.description:
More and more people ask ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity or Google’s AI Overviews instead of scrolling a page of blue links — and an assistant names one or two businesses in its answer, not ten. AI Rank Suite tells you whether yours is one of them, and fixes the things on your site that decide it.

That is the whole idea. An assistant does not “rank” your pages. It fetches a handful of URLs, reads them, and writes one answer. Four things decide whether you are in that answer, and this plugin is built around all four — with a complete classic SEO toolkit alongside, because Google still sends the clicks you have today.

1. Can an assistant find the right pages?

An AI crawler pulls a few URLs per question, not your whole site. llms.txt is the one file where you choose which few.

  • llms.txt and llms-full.txt, generated from your own content and served at your site root
  • Pin your most important pages to the top, in the order you want them read — not in date order
  • One sentence of meaning attached to every link, so the file explains your site instead of just listing it
  • A live token count, so the file never grows past what a model will actually read
  • Preferred citation, contact and content-usage lines that a model reads word for word
  • Control 31 named AI crawlers individually — OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Perplexity, Apple, Meta, Amazon, Mistral, plus ByteDance/Doubao, Baidu/ERNIE, Alibaba/Qwen, Huawei, Tencent and DeepSeek. Allow the ones you want citing you, block the ones you don’t.
  • Where a vendor publishes no crawler name, the plugin says so instead of selling you a rule that cannot be enforced

2. Can it read what it finds?

Models read in chunks. A page with descriptive subheadings, a self-contained opening paragraph and a few lists or tables survives being summarised. A wall of prose does not.

  • An AI score for every page, next to the classic SEO score, in the editor sidebar and the classic meta box
  • Concrete checks, not a vague grade: does the opening paragraph answer the question in the first 40 words, is there roughly one subheading per 300 words, are any paragraphs over 120 words, are there lists or tables, is there a question-style heading, is this page even in your llms.txt
  • Every check comes with the fix and what it is worth
  • A site-wide list of every page and its score, filtered by what is actually broken — weak scores, missing descriptions, thin content, accidentally noindexed
  • Runs on your own server. No AI key needed for any of the scoring.

3. Will it quote you by name?

An answer needs a source it can name and a fact it can trust.

  • Structured data across 77 schema.org types — Article, Product, Service, FAQ, HowTo, Recipe, Event, JobPosting, Course, Review, VideoObject, Person, LocalBusiness and more — set per page or as site-wide rules
  • Local SEO with 97 LocalBusiness types, opening hours and multiple locations
  • Open Graph and Twitter cards, social profiles, per-platform share images
  • Automatic FAQ, speakable and video structured data from what is already on the page

4. Is it actually working?

Everything above is a guess until you check it.

  • AI Answer Simulation (Pro). Write the questions your customers really ask (“who does company formation in Dubai?”), and the plugin puts them to an AI model and reads the answer back: were you named, how early in the answer, in what tone, and who was named instead of you.
  • Up to 25 monitored questions and 10 tracked competitors
  • Every run is stored, so it becomes a trend line rather than a one-off screenshot
  • Honest about what it is: a repeatable simulation against the AI model you configure. It is not a live scrape of the ChatGPT, Gemini or Perplexity apps, and nobody can promise you that.

And everything you expect from an SEO plugin

  • Title and meta description templates, site-wide and per content type, with a live Google result preview
  • XML sitemaps, plus news and video sitemaps, and an HTML sitemap block for readers
  • Robots control per page, per archive, and a full robots.txt editor
  • Google Search Console positions, Google Analytics 4, Matomo, Microsoft Clarity and PageSpeed Insights
  • Instant indexing through IndexNow (Bing, Yandex, Seznam, Naver) and the Google Indexing API
  • (Pro) A rank tracker with position history, and Bing Webmaster Tools alongside Search Console
  • (Pro) Backlink monitoring from real referrer traffic, with optional connections to Ahrefs, Semrush, Moz, Majestic, Sistrix, DataForSEO and seven SERP APIs
  • (Pro) Broken, redirected and unreachable link checking across the whole site
  • A redirect manager with regular expressions and CSV import/export, plus a 404 monitor
  • (Pro) An internal link graph — what links to what, how deep each page sits, which pages are orphans — computed entirely on your own server
  • Breadcrumbs, image alt text and title templates, canonical control, cornerstone pages
  • WooCommerce product schema (free), plus Google Merchant Center and Meta catalog feeds (Pro)
  • A cookie consent banner with Google Consent Mode v2, in opt-in (GDPR), opt-out (CCPA) or automatic mode
  • (Pro) Scheduled email reports you can put your own agency branding on

You do not have to switch SEO plugins to try this

This is the part most people ask about first. AI Rank Suite is built to run beside Yoast, Rank Math, All in One SEO, SEOPress, The SEO Framework, Slim Seo, Squirrly, WPSSO, Schema Pro or Jetpack, not instead of them.

Turn it on and, by default, your existing SEO plugin keeps doing exactly what it does today — titles, descriptions, canonicals, Open Graph, its own schema. AI Rank Suite adds only the layer nothing else on your site is doing: llms.txt, AI crawler control, AI page scoring and AI Answer Simulation. Every part of your page’s <head> gets exactly one owner, checked on the rendered page, so you never end up with two titles or two sets of structured data.

When you are ready to consolidate, one setting hands the whole <head> over. And if you want to move your existing work across first, the importer reads Yoast, Rank Math, All in One SEO, SEOPress, The SEO Framework, Slim SEO, Squirrly, SmartCrawl, Genesis, Jetpack, SEO Ultimate, WP Meta SEO, Redirection and WooCommerce — without deactivating or modifying the source plugin, filling only empty fields by default, and with an undo journal for every run.

Built for real sites

  • Measured on a 50,000-post fixture: the analyzer, the link graph, the sitemaps and every admin screen hold up
  • Long jobs (scoring, imports, the link graph, bulk work) run in resumable background batches with their own indexed tables — a timeout resumes where it stopped instead of starting over
  • Works with WPML, Polylang, TranslatePress and Weglot, including the two different shapes those plugins use for translations
  • Detects and reads Elementor, Divi, Beaver Builder, Bricks, Oxygen, WPBakery, ACF, The Events Calendar, WP Recipe Maker, WP Job Manager and more, so builder-rendered content is scored and put in your sitemaps
  • SEO fields appear inside Elementor’s own Page Settings, writing to the same values as the block editor sidebar
  • Every module can be switched off, and a disabled module loads no code at all
  • Your settings and data are kept when you deactivate or uninstall, unless you explicitly ask for them to be removed

Free vs Pro

Free, forever. Nothing in the free plugin expires, counts down, or stops working, and none of it needs an API key:

  • Titles, meta descriptions and templates with a live Google preview
  • Open Graph, Twitter cards, social profiles
  • XML, news, video and HTML sitemaps
  • All 77 schema.org types, Local SEO with opening hours and locations
  • llms.txt and llms-full.txt, checked against Google’s own Agentic Browsing rules
  • Individual control over 31 named AI crawlers, with a served-file verifier
  • The AI readiness score for every page — computed on your server, no key
  • The full site audit and the content list with its filters
  • Redirects with regex and CSV import/export, plus the 404 monitor
  • Breadcrumbs, robots.txt editor, image SEO, canonicals
  • All 14 importers — Yoast, Rank Math, AIOSEO, SEOPress and the rest — with undo
  • WooCommerce product schema; WPML, Polylang, TranslatePress, Weglot
  • Search Console, GA4, Matomo, Clarity and PageSpeed connections
  • Cookie consent banner with Google Consent Mode v2

Pro adds the features that write with AI on your own key, and the measurement moat:

  • AI Answer Simulation — 25 questions, trend line, share of voice, who was named instead of you
  • AI Autopilot — writes every missing description, title, FAQ and alt text, with a full undo
  • AI writing on your own key: descriptions, titles, FAQs, alt text, schema, translations
  • Insights: trends, movers, issue leaderboard
  • Rank tracker and keyword planner
  • Backlink monitoring that re-reads the linking page
  • Broken-link checker and internal link graph with suggestions
  • Bulk editing, catalog feeds for Merchant Center and Meta
  • Third-party SEO data providers (Ahrefs, Semrush, Moz, DataForSEO and more)
  • Scheduled white-label email reports

Pro is sold per year through Freemius, starting at one site, with updates and support included, and a 14-day money-back guarantee. Details and pricing: https://airanksuite.com

External services

This plugin can talk to the third-party services below. None of them are contacted unless you switch that feature on and supply your own credentials or identifier. With a fresh install and nothing entered, the plugin makes no outbound requests except the ones WordPress itself makes. For each service: what it is for, what is sent and when, and its terms and privacy policy.

  • AI providers (Pro): OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, Mistral, xAI, Perplexity, Groq, Cohere, Azure OpenAI, DeepSeek, Qwen, and any OpenAI-compatible endpoint including a local Ollama, LM Studio or vLLM. Used only when you enter an API key, and only for the actions you trigger: generating descriptions, titles, FAQs, alt text or schema, and running AI Answer Simulation. What is sent: the text of the page you are working on, after e-mail addresses, phone numbers, shortcodes, scripts and anything you wrap in [airanksuite-private] have been stripped out. Your key is stored encrypted. Terms and privacy: OpenAI https://openai.com/policies/terms-of-use and https://openai.com/policies/privacy-policy; Anthropic https://www.anthropic.com/legal/consumer-terms and https://www.anthropic.com/legal/privacy; Google https://policies.google.com/terms and https://policies.google.com/privacy; Mistral https://legal.mistral.ai/ and https://legal.mistral.ai/terms/privacy-policy/; xAI https://x.ai/legal/terms-of-service and https://x.ai/legal/privacy-policy; Perplexity https://www.perplexity.ai/hub/legal/terms-of-service and https://www.perplexity.ai/hub/legal/privacy-notice; Groq https://groq.com/terms-of-use and https://groq.com/privacy-policy; Cohere https://cohere.com/terms-of-use and https://cohere.com/privacy; Microsoft Azure https://azure.microsoft.com/support/legal and https://privacy.microsoft.com/privacystatement; DeepSeek https://cdn.deepseek.com/policies/en-US/deepseek-terms-of-use.html and https://cdn.deepseek.com/policies/en-US/deepseek-privacy-policy.html; Alibaba Qwen https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/legal and https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/privacy-policy. A self-hosted endpoint sends data only to the server you named.
  • Google Search Console API and Google Analytics Data API (www.googleapis.com, analyticsdata.googleapis.com, analyticsadmin.googleapis.com, oauth2.googleapis.com, accounts.google.com): read-only, to show your search positions and traffic, and only after you connect a Google account — either with “Sign in with Google” (next entry) or with your own Google Cloud OAuth credentials. Sent: your OAuth token and the property you selected, each time the report screens load or the daily snapshot runs. https://policies.google.com/terms and https://policies.google.com/privacy
  • AI Rank Suite connect service (airanksuite.com/google-connect), run by us, the authors of this plugin: used only if you press “Sign in with Google” instead of entering your own Google Cloud credentials. It holds the Google OAuth client, so that you do not have to create a Google Cloud project. Sent when you press the button: your site address, the plugin version and a one-time random value that ties the answer to your browser. Sent afterwards, whenever Google’s access token has expired and a report needs a new one: your site address and the refresh token Google issued for your connection. It receives none of your Search Console or Analytics data. Those requests go from your site to Google directly. Disconnecting, or entering your own credentials, stops all contact.   • Google tag / Google Analytics 4 (www.googletagmanager.com): if you enter a measurement ID, the Google tag is loaded on your public pages and visitors’ page views are reported to Google, subject to the consent banner you configure. https://policies.google.com/terms and https://policies.google.com/privacy
  • Google PageSpeed Insights API (www.googleapis.com): sends a page URL of yours to Google to fetch its performance score, only when you press the button. https://developers.google.com/speed/docs/insights/v5/get-started, https://policies.google.com/terms and https://policies.google.com/privacy

  • Google Places API (places.googleapis.com): only in Local SEO, with your own key, to look up your business listing when you press the button. https://cloud.google.com/maps-platform/terms and https://policies.google.com/privacy
  • OpenStreetMap Nominatim (nominatim.openstreetmap.org): only in Local SEO, and only when you press “Find coordinates from the address”. It returns the latitude and longitude for your LocalBusiness markup; no key is needed. sections.installation:
1. In WordPress, go to Plugins → Add New, search for AI Rank Suite, and click Install Now, then Activate. Or upload the plugin folder to /wp-content/plugins/ and activate it from the Plugins screen.
  2. The setup wizard opens on first activation. It takes about three minutes and every step writes real settings — nothing is a preview.
  3. If you already run another SEO plugin, the wizard detects it and defaults to running alongside it. You do not have to deactivate anything. Optionally, import your titles, descriptions, redirects and settings from it on the same screen.
  4. On the llms.txt screen, turn the file on and pin the five or ten pages you most want an assistant to read. Check it at https://yoursite.com/llms.txt.
  5. On the AI Crawlers screen, decide which AI crawlers may read your site.
  6. On the Content screen, press Analyze to score every page. This runs in the background; you can leave the screen.
  7. Optional: on the AI Engine screen, add an API key from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google or any OpenAI-compatible provider if you want AI writing and AI Answer Simulation. Everything else works without one.

Requirements: WordPress 6.4 or newer and PHP 8.1 or newer. The plugin will not load on older PHP and will tell you so rather than fataling.
sections.faq:
Does this replace Yoast or Rank Math?

It can, but it does not have to, and on day one it does not. If another SEO plugin is active, AI Rank Suite defaults to adding only the AI-search layer — llms.txt, AI crawler control, AI page scoring, AI Answer Simulation — and leaves your titles, descriptions, canonicals, Open Graph and schema exactly as they are. Nothing about your current search results changes.

If you later want one plugin instead of two, switch the compatibility mode to let AI Rank Suite own the whole <head>, import your settings and content fields from the other plugin, and then deactivate it. Doing it in that order means you never have a gap.

Can I really run it with Rank Math (or Yoast, or AIOSEO) installed at the same time?

Yes, and that is the intended way to start. Every part of the page head — title, description, canonical, robots, Open Graph, Twitter cards, JSON-LD, hreflang — is assigned exactly one owner, and the assignment is enforced on the finished HTML rather than by hoping the two plugins use different hooks. So you will not get duplicate titles or two competing sets of structured data. Detection covers Yoast, Rank Math, All in One SEO, SEOPress, The SEO Framework, Slim Seo, Squirrly, WPSSO, Schema Pro and Jetpack.

Do I need an OpenAI or Claude API key?

No, and most of the plugin never asks for one. Page scoring, llms.txt, schema, sitemaps, the link checker, redirects, the internal link graph, Search Console, indexing, imports — all of it runs without any AI key, entirely on your own server.

A key is needed for exactly two things: AI writing (descriptions, titles, FAQs, alt text, schema suggestions) and AI Answer Simulation. You bring your own key from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Mistral, xAI, Groq, DeepSeek, Qwen, Azure OpenAI, OpenRouter or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint — including a model running locally through Ollama, LM Studio or vLLM, in which case nothing leaves your machine at all.

What does it cost to run if I do use AI?

You pay your AI provider directly at their list price; the plugin adds nothing on top. To keep that from being a surprise, the plugin estimates the cost of a job before you run it, records the actual cost after, and enforces spending limits — out of the box, $10 a day, $100 a month, and $25 for any single bulk job, with a hard stop when a limit is hit. You can change or remove all three.

In practice: a meta description on a small model costs a fraction of a cent, so writing descriptions for a few hundred pages is a coffee. AI Answer Simulation is the more expensive one because it asks a full model a real question — budget for it per run, not per page.

What is llms.txt, and does anything actually read it?

llms.txt is a plain markdown file at the root of your site — yoursite.com/llms.txt — that tells an AI system what your site is, which pages matter, and how you want to be credited. Think of it as robots.txt’s opposite: robots.txt says what not to read, llms.txt says what to read first.

Honest answer on adoption: it is a proposed convention, not a ratified standard, and no AI vendor has publicly committed to honouring it. It costs you nothing to publish, it is trivially cheap to serve, and if the convention holds you are already there. The plugin also produces llms-full.txt, which contains the actual text of your chosen pages as markdown — useful today for anyone who feeds your site to a model deliberately. Neither file is the whole strategy, which is why page structure, schema and measurement are the other three quarters of this plugin.

Does it work on a multilingual site?

Yes. WPML, Polylang, TranslatePress and Weglot are supported, including the two different ways they work — WPML and Polylang give each translation its own post, TranslatePress and Weglot translate one post on the fly. Pages are scored, listed and sitemapped per language, the content list filters by language, and hreflang is handled. The admin interface itself is available in English and German.

Will it cope with a large site?

It is built for that case specifically. Every long-running job — page scoring, imports, the internal link graph, bulk edits, the link checker — runs as a resumable background job in its own indexed database tables, processing a slice at a time. A PHP timeout or a killed request resumes at the cursor rather than starting again. The link graph and the URL inventory were measured on a 50,000-post fixture with over 700,000 internal links inside a 128 MB memory limit, and every admin screen was checked at that size.

If your host is aggressive about request limits, everything continues on the next tick. Nothing here depends on WP-Cron running reliably.

Is my content or data sent anywhere?

Only where you send it. With no keys configured, nothing leaves your server.

When you do use an AI feature, the page’s text is sent to the provider you chose, and only after e-mail addresses, phone numbers, shortcodes, HTML comments, scripts and anything you wrap in [airanksuite-private]…[/airs-private] are stripped out — the preview tells you exactly what was removed before anything is sent. Page content is also framed as untrusted data in the prompt, so text on one of your pages cannot issue instructions to the model.

Your API keys are stored encrypted at rest. All scoring, the link graph, link suggestions, sitemaps, schema and the audits run locally with no external call at all. The full list of services and what each one receives is in the External services section above.

What happens to my data if I deactivate or uninstall?

Nothing is deleted. Settings, scores, redirects, keywords and history are kept by default so that deactivating to test something, or reinstalling, never costs you work. If you genuinely want everything removed, there is an explicit switch for it under Settings → Data, and only then does uninstalling clear the plugin’s options and tables.

Will this make ChatGPT recommend my business?

No plugin can promise that, and you should be wary of any that does. What this one does is remove the reasons an assistant would not: it makes your pages retrievable, gives them a structure a model can summarise without mangling, states in machine-readable form what your business is and how to cite it, and then measures whether your name shows up in answers to the questions you care about. The measurement is the point — you get a trend line rather than a hunch.

Does it slow my site down?

The front end does very little: meta tags, JSON-LD and the redirect check, all from cached values. Sitemaps, llms.txt and catalog feeds are cached and served from rewrite rules, not built on each request. The heavy work — scoring, crawling links, building the graph — happens in the admin as background jobs, never in a visitor’s request. Any module you do not use can be switched off completely, and a disabled module loads no code.

I run WooCommerce. What do I get?

Product structured data with prices, availability, brand and reviews (including from Judge.me, Yotpo and the common brand plugins), a Google Merchant Center feed and a Meta / Instagram catalog feed served from cached URLs those platforms can poll, and a catalog audit that tells you which products are missing the fields those feeds require. The Catalog Feeds screen only appears when WooCommerce is active.

Can I give a client or an editor limited access?

Access follows WordPress itself: the plugin’s screens and routes are for administrators, and a route that names a post also asks WordPress whether this user may read or edit that post. The plugin no longer ships capabilities of its own.

I’m migrating from another SEO plugin. Will I lose my work?

The importer reads Yoast, Rank Math, All in One SEO, SEOPress, The SEO Framework, Slim SEO, Squirrly, SmartCrawl, Genesis, Jetpack, SEO Ultimate, WP Meta SEO, Redirection and WooCommerce. It never modifies or deactivates the source plugin, so your old setup stays intact and reversible. By default it fills only fields that are empty here and tells you exactly how many values it left alone and why; every run is logged and can be undone. It also imports redirects from a CSV or JSON handover file, previewing what it would do before it does it.

Does it support the block editor and page builders?

Both. SEO and AI fields appear in the block editor sidebar, in the classic meta box, and inside Elementor’s own Page Settings — all three writing to the same values. Content rendered by Divi, Beaver Builder, Bricks, Oxygen, WPBakery, Elementor and ACF is read for scoring and sitemaps, so builder-heavy pages are not scored as if they were empty.
sections.changelog:
0.2.49

  • The classic WordPress screen. Text fields, selects and text areas are now core’s own: 40 pixels tall, a 2 pixel corner, the grey hairline, 14 point type, and core’s focus ring. Labels sit above them at 14/600 like a settings screen, with the description underneath in core’s grey.
  • Tables read as a WordPress list table: a hairline frame, a quiet header with a rule under it, alternating rows and a hover.
  • Notices have core’s shape, with no corner and no shadow, a four pixel coloured edge, and a tint mixed from that edge so the dark theme gets a dark tint instead of a bright one.

0.2.48

  • A page now says what changed about it. Every analysis records the two scores, and the report states the first reading against the latest one: “+37 on the AI score since 19 October, over 4 measurements”. Until now every number described the page as it is today, which made an evening spent rewriting descriptions unprovable. A re-analysis that produces the same scores writes nothing, and the first reading is never dropped, because the baseline is the whole meaning of “before”.
  • The stylesheet is readable again. .ars-hero was defined six times, .ars-tab five, .ars-btn-primary four; each is one block now, 158 lines lighter. Nothing changed on screen, and that is measured rather than claimed: the computed style of 1,670 elements across ten screens in light and dark is identical before and after.
  • A test fails the build if a selector is written more than twice again, and four tests cover the score history.

0.2.47

  • The dashboard counts rules, not findings. A site of 2,538 pages reported “17,733 open findings”, which is a wall rather than a number. The same run came from twelve rules. A rule is the unit of work, because one fix to a template clears every page it touches, so the tile now reads “12 / 38 rules failing” and keeps the finding count as the explanation underneath.
  • The audit verdict says the same thing: “2 critical rules are costing you search traffic today”, with the findings, pages, warnings and notices behind it.
  • How many rules exist now comes from the rule catalogue. The audit screen carried const RULES = 30, which was right when it was written and had been wrong for a while: there are 38.
  • 458 German translations that were in the catalogue but had never reached the admin screens are there now, and two plural forms that had regressed to English are German again.

0.2.46

  • The admin takes its colour from WordPress. Whatever admin colour scheme you run, the plugin’s buttons, tabs, toggles and charts arrive in it. The accent is measured from one of WordPress’s own buttons at load, so Midnight stays Midnight and Sunrise stays Sunrise, on any WordPress version.
  • Buttons, second-level tabs and card headers use core’s own geometry instead of a set of their own: core’s radius, core’s weight, core’s sub-tab row with its rule.
  • The dashboard opens with what to do, not with what is missing. The three next actions moved above the status, and the agent floor, which drew seven connection cards and ten job rows all reading “no engine”, now appears only once an engine is connected. The same sentence used to be on the screen five times.
  • Fewer places to look. Measure went from seven screens to five: Insights is a tab of Overview, and the data providers are a tab of Backlinks. Import and backup is a tab of Settings. The developer reference is there when WP_DEBUG is on, when the airanksuite_show_developer_tools filter asks for it, or from the All settings index, and its address keeps working either way.

0.2.45

  • The plugin’s own capabilities no longer guard anything. Every REST route and every screen asks WordPress directly, and the capability stands in the route itself: current_user_can( 'manage_options' ). Routes that name a post also ask WordPress about that post.
  • The Roles screen is gone with them. It handed out four capabilities that now decide nothing, and an installation that still carries them has them removed on update. Access follows WordPress roles: administrators manage the plugin.
  • A test fails the build if a route is registered without a WordPress capability on the spot, or if one of the old capabilities is checked anywhere.

0.2.44

  • Every REST route now asks WordPress for one of its own capabilities before the plugin capability is considered. A plugin capability can be handed to any role in Settings, Roles, so it can never be the only gate.
  • Values read from $_SERVER and $_COOKIE are sanitized, not only unslashed.
  • The audit export hands spreadsheet rows to the browser, which writes the file. Nothing is echoed from the route, and a cell that starts with an equals sign is written as text, so a spreadsheet cannot run it as a formula.
  • llms.txt is stripped of markup on output.

0.2.43

  • Elementor no longer overwrites a title applied elsewhere. Elementor keeps its own copy of the SEO title, description, keyword and noindex switch in its page settings and posts all of them on every save, layout edits included. Written back as they came, that copy put the old title back over one applied minutes earlier from the AI review, the block-editor sidebar or the content list. The panel now remembers what it handed the builder and writes only the fields that were changed inside Elementor. The meta box and the block-editor sidebar already behaved this way; a test now holds all three to it.

  • Long keyword lists fold. A page can carry a hundred keywords, and the meta box and the sidebar drew every one of them as a chip, a wall that pushed the page down and a counter that read “100 / 10”. Both now show the first twelve (eight in the sidebar), one chip says how many more there are, and the opened list scrolls inside a box. The limit reads 100, which is what it always was.

0.2.42

  • The SEO score is a formula. Four pillars with fixed points, one hundred in total: keyword 40 (in the title, the description, the URL, the first paragraph, a subheading, the density and an image alt), title and description 25, structure 20 (one H1, heading order, 300+ words, alt texts, a compact slug), links 15. Until now the keyword checks fed no score at all, so a page with the keyword nowhere scored like one with it everywhere. Without a focus keyword the keyword pillar earns nothing and the score cannot pass 60. The four numbers are shown under the rings in the editor sidebar and the meta box.
  • llms.txt written in one click. “Write everything” gives every page in both files a summary (from the AI engine when a key is stored, from the page’s first sentences otherwise), writes the site’s lead paragraph and rebuilds both files, with a progress bar. Pages that already have a summary are kept unless you choose to rewrite.
  • Site Audit: seven more rules, a way out of every finding, and a spreadsheet. Meta description length, missing focus keyword, keyword missing from the title, very long slug, post without a featured image, no internal links out, oversized featured image. Every finding links to the optimiser as well as to the editor, and the whole run exports as CSV.
  • Measure has an overview. Search Console and Analytics for the same days side by side, each against the same days before, the two lines on one axis, the top pages with both numbers. Bing sits next to Google: the Search Console property beside the site Bing expects, with Bing’s import from Search Console one click away.
  • Image SEO counts the media library. How many images have no alt text, are wider than 2500 pixels or heavier than 500 KB, the largest ones listed, and one run that writes the missing alt texts from the template, fifty at a time.
  • Import shows what is there. The plugin that is installed or left data behind gets a card with the numbers and the buttons; the rest are one line each. Yoast and SEOPress have their marks.
  • The AI proposal compares against the page as it is now. “Now” in the title and description review showed the snapshot the proposal had taken when it was written; after an earlier apply that was an old title, and the content list, reading the page, showed the real one. The review now reads the current values with every load and says when the metadata changed since the proposal.
  • Job postings carry what Google’s report asks for. datePosted from the post date, a job ID, the applicant country for remote jobs, and whether applying happens on the page.

0.2.41

  • The Pro package carries its translations again. The 0.2.40 Pro build shipped without the languages folder, so every screen fell back to English on a German site. The build now refuses to run without the translation sources, and the release check verifies that the compiled catalogues are in the package.
  • The word counter is called Words again. The tab under Content had been renamed Length; the counter of every page’s words, and of the whole site, is the same tab and now says so.

0.2.40

  • The dashboard takes a score reading itself. WP-Cron only runs when somebody visits the site, so on a quiet site the daily reading added in 0.2.39 could wait for days. When the dashboard opens and the last reading is older than twenty hours, it takes one on the spot. The findings card gained a button: “Run an audit now” starts one and opens Site Audit, where it runs slice by slice.
  • The editor toolbar shows both scores. The pinned AI Rank Suite button carries GEO and SEO as two small pills in their verdict colours, and it sits first in the pinned row. With Rank Math active, its two pinned score buttons step back into the ⋮ menu, where its sidebar still opens, so the toolbar holds one set of numbers instead of two.
  • Keywords in bulk. The keyword field in the meta box and in the sidebar accepts a pasted list (commas, semicolons or line breaks) and adds every entry at once, and the AI suggestions have an “Add all” button. Ten remains the ceiling.
  • The meta box and the sidebar look like WordPress. Core blue for every button, the secondary as an outline of the same blue, 3 and 4 pixel corners, core input borders, no gradients and no tinted shadows. The score rings are honey rather than marigold, and the number sits in the centre of the ring in every browser: it is HTML laid over the ring now, not SVG text rotated back into place.
  • The post list says what Rank Math says. The SEO details column adds the schema type the page will carry and three link counts as icons: internal, external and incoming. Score pills are top-aligned like every other cell, so they stay next to the title when another column makes the row tall.

0.2.39

  • The AI search score is read once a day. The dashboard’s “AI search score over time” card promised one point per recalculation, by hand or on schedule, and only the first half was true: a point was stamped when somebody pressed Recalculate, and on a site where nobody did, the line’s last date stayed where it was for weeks. A daily job (airanksuite_job_score_snapshot, listed under Autopilot’s systems) now takes a reading, so the line moves on its own. Recalculate still adds a point on the spot.
  • Both trend cards say when they last moved and when they move next. Under the score card: the last reading and the next automatic one. Under the findings card: the last completed audit and the next scheduled one, or, when none is scheduled, that an audit has to be run or scheduled for the line to gain a point. A last label from three weeks ago is a schedule now, not a fault.
  • The “Open findings” tile updates with the chart under it. Finishing an audit cleared the chart’s cache but not the tile’s, so for up to five minutes the chart showed the new run while the tile kept the old count.

0.2.38

  • Recurring events are scheduled on init, not on plugins_loaded. Scheduling an event asks every plugin for its list of cron schedules, and WooCommerce translates the label of its schedules while answering. Asked during our boot, that made WooCommerce load its translations before init, which WordPress 6.7 and later report as a notice under WP_DEBUG, against this plugin. All eight recurring events (job resumer, retention, rank snapshots, backlink checks, listing refresh, reports, audit alerts, AI visibility) now go through one helper, Cron::ensure(), that waits for init. On a site without WooCommerce nothing changes; on a site with it the notice is gone.
  • Running an import needs a WordPress administrator. 0.2.37 added that check to the settings import and the backup restore, and left it off the plugin importer, which can replace settings, redirects and post data just the same. Starting, ticking and cancelling an import run, and reading an uploaded file, now require manage_options as well. Listing the sources, detecting installed plugins, exporting and reading the backup stay with the plugin’s own capability.

0.2.37

  • Changing who may do what needs a WordPress administrator. The plugin has its own capabilities so that an agency can hand “manage settings” to an editor. That capability alone also opened the role editor, so somebody who had been given it could have given it, or anything else the plugin offers, to further roles. The role editor now requires WordPress’ own promote_users as well. The same second check, manage_options, was added to the other routes that reach beyond the plugin’s settings: writing and restoring .htaccess, importing a settings file, restoring a settings backup, the maintenance tasks under Developer tools, and creating, changing or testing a webhook, which sends site data to an address somebody typed in. WordPress is asked first, so a refused request does not use up the rate limit. For an administrator nothing changes.
  • Values reach JavaScript as JSON. The toolbar’s script received its REST address and nonce by text substitution into the source, and the Matomo snippet had its address and site id pasted between quotes. Both now get one JSON object built by wp_json_encode(). The addresses were the site’s own, so nothing could be injected, but a value that is encoded for a URL is not encoded for a script, and only one of the two is right.
  • Structured data is printed with the default JSON encoding. The JSON-LD in the page head was encoded with flags that leave slashes and non-ASCII characters as they are. With the defaults every slash is escaped, so no headline can close the script element, and the output is the same data to every consumer.
  • Six importer queries pass the table name as an identifier. The readers for Redirection, Rank Math and All in One SEO appended the other plugin’s table name to the statement. It travels as %i now, like everywhere else.

0.2.36

  • Everything the plugin names is named airanksuite now. Options, tables, post and term meta, capabilities, scheduled events, hooks, constants, the REST namespace (airanksuite/v1), script handles and the WP-CLI command (wp airanksuite) used a four-letter abbreviation that the directory’s review found too short to be safe from collisions with other plugins. Your data moves by itself: on the first request after the update, before any setting is read, tables are renamed, options and meta keys are carried across, capabilities and scheduled events follow. Nothing is copied row by row and nothing is left behind under the old names. Shortcodes already typed into pages, such as [airs_breadcrumbs] and [airs_business_hours], keep working under their old names as well as the new ones, and so does the [airs-private] marker. A settings export or a pre-update backup made by an earlier version restores under today’s names. If you wrote code against the old hooks, constants or REST paths, replace airs with airanksuite in it.
  • A route that names a post asks WordPress about that post. A plugin capability says what somebody may do with the plugin, not which posts they may see. Reading a post’s schema or its PageSpeed result needed only “view reports”, so a role with that capability could read them for a colleague’s private draft. Those routes now require read_post on the post itself, and writing requires edit_post. The same check was added where a post id arrives in the body or in a list: applying an internal link suggestion, rejecting or undoing an Autopilot proposal, a bulk run over chosen ids, submitting a URL for indexing. The Autopilot queue and log, the content list and its CSV leave out drafts the current user could not open in WordPress.
  • No SQL statement is assembled any more. The redirect list built its ORDER BY from the sort the screen asked for. The value came from an allow-list, so it was never injectable, but a statement put together from pieces cannot be told apart from one that is. Every list in the plugin now sends one constant statement: the sort column travels as an identifier placeholder, the direction selects one of two literals, and a filter that is not in use is switched off by a flag instead of being left out of the text. Same results, same order, same paging.
  • The sitemap’s browser view is a file. The XSL stylesheet behind /sitemap.xsl, CSS included, was a string inside the PHP source; it is assets/sitemap/sitemap.xsl now, and PHP only serves it.
  • No translation is loaded before init. A cron interval label was translated while modules scheduled their events on plugins_loaded, which WordPress 6.7 and later report as a notice under WP_DEBUG. The interval was a copy of WordPress’ own weekly and is gone.
  • Four services were missing from the list of external services, and are documented with what is sent, when, and their terms and privacy policies: OpenStreetMap Nominatim (“Find coordinates from the address” in Local SEO), our own connect service behind “Sign in with Google”, the Google Ads API (Pro keyword ideas), and the webhooks you configure yourself.

0.2.35

  • Every database query goes through $wpdb->prepare(). 107 reads and writes were built as strings with the table name interpolated and no placeholder at all. None carried user input, but a query that is not prepared cannot be told apart from one that should have been, and the directory’s review said so. Table names are now passed as %i identifiers, IN lists get one placeholder per value, and LIKE patterns go through esc_like(); nothing is pasted into SQL by hand any more.
  • No plugin CSS is printed into the page. The upgrade menu entry’s colour, the boot skeleton behind the admin app, the upgrade screen’s stylesheet and the post-list score columns were each an echoed
  • The head arbiter cannot leave its output buffer open. If another plugin opened a buffer above ours and never closed it, finish() gave up and the plugin’s own ob_start() stayed open for the rest of the request. Foreign buffers are flushed through first now, and a shutdown guard closes ours if nothing else did.
  • The admin app never guesses where admin-ajax.php is. The endpoint always came from PHP, but the script kept a literal /wp-admin/admin-ajax.php as a last resort, which is wrong on every renamed or subdirectory admin. The fallback is gone.
  • The compiled admin and editor bundles ship with their source. assets/admin/src and assets/editor/src, the two Vite configs and the build steps in the readme, so anyone can read or rebuild what runs.
  • Every external service is documented with its terms and privacy policy, host by host: the Google APIs, the Google tag, IndexNow and its four endpoints, Bing Webmaster Tools, Microsoft Clarity, Matomo, Places, PageSpeed, the AI providers and the SEO data providers.
  • One review platform that has withdrawn API access from all plugins no longer appears in the local directory suggestions.
  • Two answer-simulation reads were behind the licence gate. The trend and the competitor matrix are reports on data already collected, and an inactive licence is meant to pause new work, never to hide what exists. Both read freely now, as every other report does.
  • A site that moves from Pro to the free edition no longer fires empty cron events. The rank snapshot, the answer simulation, the e-mail report and the backlink re-check stayed in the cron table with nothing listening, so WordPress ran them into nothing on schedule for ever. Any scheduled event of this plugin’s with no module behind it is removed once, the first time the plugin loads after the change.
  • The free edition’s admin no longer asks for routes it does not have. The dashboard card, the content screen, the analyzer and the licence tab each requested an endpoint that only exists with a Pro module installed and left a 404 in the browser console; each asks the module list first now, and the licence tab says what the free edition is instead of reading a licence that cannot exist.
  • The 404 monitor explains what it records and where an entry goes, instead of showing one line when it is empty.
  • The free edition never ran its uninstall cleanup. The Pro build wires it to Freemius’ own uninstall hook inside a file the free package does not carry, so the “remove my data on uninstall” setting there was a switch connected to nothing. The free edition registers WordPress’ uninstall hook itself now; data is still kept unless you opted out of keeping it.
  • Nine explanatory captions added in 0.2.34 (the score ring, the four counters, the three trend notes, the directories hint in Local SEO) had no German translation and showed in English on German sites. They have one now.

0.2.34

  • The dashboard says what it is connected to, and what is being done with AI. The card that reports the agent now carries the wiring underneath it: a row of every service the plugin is plugged into — the AI engines, Search Console, Matomo, Analytics, Bing, IndexNow, WooCommerce — each with what stops working while it is dark, fed by one moving artery that carries current only while an engine can actually answer. Under it, the ten kinds of work the plugin does with a model and which engine each one goes to. It is drawn with or without a key: without one, the same diagram greys out, which is the argument for connecting one.
  • Every figure now says what it counts. Calls today, spend today, the run’s progress, the run’s cost, an engine’s load, the score in the ring, pages scored, open findings, broken links and each of the three trend lines carry one sentence explaining what is measured, over what window, and whether the number is metered or forecast.
  • Five figures were measuring the wrong thing. “Calls today” and “Spent today” counted from UTC midnight while the site keeps its own clock, so in the Gulf every morning until 4am reported the wrong day. A finished run went on advertising the estimate it opened with instead of the metered cost of the calls it actually made, and showed a full progress bar beside the word “idle”. The search clicks sparkline selected the oldest thirty snapshots, so on any site with more history it froze on its first month for ever. The findings line plotted a run that was still crawling, drawing a cliff that reversed itself an hour later, and labelled its points in UTC while the score line beside it used the site’s timezone. The coverage line bucketed its days in UTC for the same reason.
  • On a translated site the desks were invisible. The panel matched each job against the translated name of its desk, so on a German or French install nothing matched and the whole lower half of the diagram rendered empty, with no error anywhere. Jobs now carry a language-independent key. The engine load bar likewise divides by a total the server sends rather than by the length of whatever list the screen happened to be holding.

0.2.33

  • The compliance work from the WordPress.org review reaches the Pro edition too. Analytics tags are enqueued rather than printed into wp_head, so they are visible to the script loader and to caching layers, and Consent Mode’s requirement that its default runs before the Google tag is a declared dependency instead of a hook priority that another plugin could land inside. The cookie banner’s stylesheet moved to the head, where it belongs, and no longer arrives after the banner it styles. Five reads of $_SERVER that carried a phpcs:ignore are sanitized through one helper that unslashes before it sanitizes.
  • The licence gate cannot be filtered into refusing. airanksuite/licensing/allows still lets a host or an agency widen access; it can no longer narrow it, so a third-party snippet cannot lock a customer out of something they have paid for.

0.2.32

  • The WordPress.org edition carries no licensing code at all. Directory guideline 5 forbids a hosted plugin from locking any feature behind a licence, and says the locked code must not even be present. The build already left the Pro modules out; it now also leaves out the licensing module, the Freemius SDK and the licence bootstrap, so no code path remains in the free package that could answer “no” to a feature. The licence gate additionally refuses to enforce anything, and refuses to be filtered into enforcing anything, without the Pro build’s own marker.
  • Analytics tags are enqueued instead of printed. The Google tag, its configuration, Microsoft Clarity, Matomo and the consent banner used to print <script> and <style> straight into wp_head, which makes them invisible to the script loader and to every caching or optimisation layer. They register handles and attach inline code now. Consent Mode’s requirement that its default runs before the Google tag is expressed as a dependency rather than a hook priority, so nothing can land between them, and the cookie banner’s stylesheet moved to the head instead of arriving after the banner it styles.
  • Request input is sanitized rather than excused. Five reads of $_SERVER were annotated with phpcs:ignore instead of being cleaned. Headers and the request URI are attacker-influenced like any other input, and they now go through one helper that unslashes before it sanitizes, in that order.
  • Translations come from the directory. WordPress.org generates and serves language packs for a hosted plugin, and a bundled catalogue silently shadows whatever the community contributes. The free package ships the .pot for translators and nothing compiled.
  • A plugin role could edit posts WordPress would not open for it. The SEO editor preset grants “edits titles, descriptions and keywords”; it never said which posts, and the content route did not ask. A user holding that capability could rewrite the SEO title, description, slug, robots and canonical of any post over the REST API, including somebody else’s private draft, and read that draft’s text and previews from the same screen. The route now makes the object check WordPress makes: edit_post before any write, read_post before an unpublished post is shown at all, and an unreadable id answers “not found” rather than confirming it exists. Two tests hold it from both sides.
  • A clean audit no longer shows the last one’s findings. The dashboard tile derived the run from the newest row in the findings table. A run that finds nothing writes no rows, so the newest row still belonged to the run before it and the number stayed up after everything was fixed; a run in progress, conversely, was counted half-finished. The tile now reads the run the auditor publishes when it completes, which is the same run the audit report shows. No finished run, no number.
  • A large redirect import cannot time out half-applied. Fifty thousand rows, each a lookup and a write, do not fit in one PHP time limit, and what a timeout left behind was some redirects live, the rest missing, and nothing on screen saying which. The import now applies two thousand rows per request and answers with where to continue; the screen walks through the slices and reports the totals as before.

0.2.31

  • The page drawer no longer runs off the right edge. On a window around 1100px wide the drawer’s own column was sized by its content rather than by the drawer, so the header chips, the tab strip and the whole right-hand rail were drawn 40px past the edge and cut off; the search preview looked clipped and the view switch broke into two rows. The drawer’s column is now an explicit track that cannot exceed the drawer, every grid inside the rail is the same, the preview frames fill the rail, and the view switch reads Google, AI answer, Social, X on one line.
  • Titles show their dash, not –. WordPress hands the admin a texturised title with the dash as an HTML entity, and the drawer header, the list row and the SEO title fallback printed it literally. Decoded once on the server, so every screen gets the same plain text.

0.2.30

  • The admin looks like WordPress again. An …

short_description: AI Rank Suite shows whether AI assistants name your site, and fixes what stops them: llms.txt, AI page scores, schema and classic SEO.
description:
More and more people ask ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity or Google’s AI Overviews instead of scrolling a page of blue links — and an assistant names one or two businesses in its answer, not ten. AI Rank Suite tells you whether yours is one of them, and fixes the things on your site that decide it.

That is the whole idea. An assistant does not “rank” your pages. It fetches a handful of URLs, reads them, and writes one answer. Four things decide whether you are in that answer, and this plugin is built around all four — with a complete classic SEO toolkit alongside, because Google still sends the clicks you have today.

1. Can an assistant find the right pages?

An AI crawler pulls a few URLs per question, not your whole site. llms.txt is the one file where you choose which few.

  • llms.txt and llms-full.txt, generated from your own content and served at your site root
  • Pin your most important pages to the top, in the order you want them read — not in date order
  • One sentence of meaning attached to every link, so the file explains your site instead of just listing it
  • A live token count, so the file never grows past what a model will actually read
  • Preferred citation, contact and content-usage lines that a model reads word for word
  • Control 31 named AI crawlers individually — OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Perplexity, Apple, Meta, Amazon, Mistral, plus ByteDance/Doubao, Baidu/ERNIE, Alibaba/Qwen, Huawei, Tencent and DeepSeek. Allow the ones you want citing you, block the ones you don’t.
  • Where a vendor publishes no crawler name, the plugin says so instead of selling you a rule that cannot be enforced

2. Can it read what it finds?

Models read in chunks. A page with descriptive subheadings, a self-contained opening paragraph and a few lists or tables survives being summarised. A wall of prose does not.

  • An AI score for every page, next to the classic SEO score, in the editor sidebar and the classic meta box
  • Concrete checks, not a vague grade: does the opening paragraph answer the question in the first 40 words, is there roughly one subheading per 300 words, are any paragraphs over 120 words, are there lists or tables, is there a question-style heading, is this page even in your llms.txt
  • Every check comes with the fix and what it is worth
  • A site-wide list of every page and its score, filtered by what is actually broken — weak scores, missing descriptions, thin content, accidentally noindexed
  • Runs on your own server. No AI key needed for any of the scoring.

3. Will it quote you by name?

An answer needs a source it can name and a fact it can trust.

  • Structured data across 77 schema.org types — Article, Product, Service, FAQ, HowTo, Recipe, Event, JobPosting, Course, Review, VideoObject, Person, LocalBusiness and more — set per page or as site-wide rules
  • Local SEO with 97 LocalBusiness types, opening hours and multiple locations
  • Open Graph and Twitter cards, social profiles, per-platform share images
  • Automatic FAQ, speakable and video structured data from what is already on the page

4. Is it actually working?

Everything above is a guess until you check it.

  • AI Answer Simulation (Pro). Write the questions your customers really ask (“who does company formation in Dubai?”), and the plugin puts them to an AI model and reads the answer back: were you named, how early in the answer, in what tone, and who was named instead of you.
  • Up to 25 monitored questions and 10 tracked competitors
  • Every run is stored, so it becomes a trend line rather than a one-off screenshot
  • Honest about what it is: a repeatable simulation against the AI model you configure. It is not a live scrape of the ChatGPT, Gemini or Perplexity apps, and nobody can promise you that.

And everything you expect from an SEO plugin

  • Title and meta description templates, site-wide and per content type, with a live Google result preview
  • XML sitemaps, plus news and video sitemaps, and an HTML sitemap block for readers
  • Robots control per page, per archive, and a full robots.txt editor
  • Google Search Console positions, Google Analytics 4, Matomo, Microsoft Clarity and PageSpeed Insights
  • Instant indexing through IndexNow (Bing, Yandex, Seznam, Naver) and the Google Indexing API
  • (Pro) A rank tracker with position history, and Bing Webmaster Tools alongside Search Console
  • (Pro) Backlink monitoring from real referrer traffic, with optional connections to Ahrefs, Semrush, Moz, Majestic, Sistrix, DataForSEO and seven SERP APIs
  • (Pro) Broken, redirected and unreachable link checking across the whole site
  • A redirect manager with regular expressions and CSV import/export, plus a 404 monitor
  • (Pro) An internal link graph — what links to what, how deep each page sits, which pages are orphans — computed entirely on your own server
  • Breadcrumbs, image alt text and title templates, canonical control, cornerstone pages
  • WooCommerce product schema (free), plus Google Merchant Center and Meta catalog feeds (Pro)
  • A cookie consent banner with Google Consent Mode v2, in opt-in (GDPR), opt-out (CCPA) or automatic mode
  • (Pro) Scheduled email reports you can put your own agency branding on

You do not have to switch SEO plugins to try this

This is the part most people ask about first. AI Rank Suite is built to run beside Yoast, Rank Math, All in One SEO, SEOPress, The SEO Framework, Slim Seo, Squirrly, WPSSO, Schema Pro or Jetpack, not instead of them.

Turn it on and, by default, your existing SEO plugin keeps doing exactly what it does today — titles, descriptions, canonicals, Open Graph, its own schema. AI Rank Suite adds only the layer nothing else on your site is doing: llms.txt, AI crawler control, AI page scoring and AI Answer Simulation. Every part of your page’s <head> gets exactly one owner, checked on the rendered page, so you never end up with two titles or two sets of structured data.

When you are ready to consolidate, one setting hands the whole <head> over. And if you want to move your existing work across first, the importer reads Yoast, Rank Math, All in One SEO, SEOPress, The SEO Framework, Slim SEO, Squirrly, SmartCrawl, Genesis, Jetpack, SEO Ultimate, WP Meta SEO, Redirection and WooCommerce — without deactivating or modifying the source plugin, filling only empty fields by default, and with an undo journal for every run.

Built for real sites

  • Measured on a 50,000-post fixture: the analyzer, the link graph, the sitemaps and every admin screen hold up
  • Long jobs (scoring, imports, the link graph, bulk work) run in resumable background batches with their own indexed tables — a timeout resumes where it stopped instead of starting over
  • Works with WPML, Polylang, TranslatePress and Weglot, including the two different shapes those plugins use for translations
  • Detects and reads Elementor, Divi, Beaver Builder, Bricks, Oxygen, WPBakery, ACF, The Events Calendar, WP Recipe Maker, WP Job Manager and more, so builder-rendered content is scored and put in your sitemaps
  • SEO fields appear inside Elementor’s own Page Settings, writing to the same values as the block editor sidebar
  • Every module can be switched off, and a disabled module loads no code at all
  • Your settings and data are kept when you deactivate or uninstall, unless you explicitly ask for them to be removed

Free vs Pro

Free, forever. Nothing in the free plugin expires, counts down, or stops working, and none of it needs an API key:

  • Titles, meta descriptions and templates with a live Google preview
  • Open Graph, Twitter cards, social profiles
  • XML, news, video and HTML sitemaps
  • All 77 schema.org types, Local SEO with opening hours and locations
  • llms.txt and llms-full.txt, checked against Google’s own Agentic Browsing rules
  • Individual control over 31 named AI crawlers, with a served-file verifier
  • The AI readiness score for every page — computed on your server, no key
  • The full site audit and the content list with its filters
  • Redirects with regex and CSV import/export, plus the 404 monitor
  • Breadcrumbs, robots.txt editor, image SEO, canonicals
  • All 14 importers — Yoast, Rank Math, AIOSEO, SEOPress and the rest — with undo
  • WooCommerce product schema; WPML, Polylang, TranslatePress, Weglot
  • Search Console, GA4, Matomo, Clarity and PageSpeed connections
  • Cookie consent banner with Google Consent Mode v2

Pro adds the features that write with AI on your own key, and the measurement moat:

  • AI Answer Simulation — 25 questions, trend line, share of voice, who was named instead of you
  • AI Autopilot — writes every missing description, title, FAQ and alt text, with a full undo

Pro is sold per year through Freemius, starting at one site, with updates and support included, and a 14-day money-back guarantee. Details and pricing: https://airanksuite.com

External services

This plugin can talk to the third-party services below. None of them are contacted unless you switch that feature on and supply your own credentials or identifier. With a fresh install and nothing entered, the plugin makes no outbound requests except the ones WordPress itself makes. For each service: what it is for, what is sent and when, and its terms and privacy policy.

  • AI providers (Pro): OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, Mistral, xAI, Perplexity, Groq, Cohere, Azure OpenAI, DeepSeek, Qwen, and any OpenAI-compatible endpoint including a local Ollama, LM Studio or vLLM. Used only when you enter an API key, and only for the actions you trigger: generating descriptions, titles, FAQs, alt text or schema, and running AI Answer Simulation. What is sent: the text of the page you are working on, after e-mail addresses, phone numbers, shortcodes, scripts and anything you wrap in [airanksuite-private] have been stripped out. Your key is stored encrypted. Terms and privacy: OpenAI https://openai.com/policies/terms-of-use and https://openai.com/policies/privacy-policy; Anthropic https://www.anthropic.com/legal/consumer-terms and https://www.anthropic.com/legal/privacy; Google https://policies.google.com/terms and https://policies.google.com/privacy; Mistral https://legal.mistral.ai/ and https://legal.mistral.ai/terms/privacy-policy/; xAI https://x.ai/legal/terms-of-service and https://x.ai/legal/privacy-policy; Perplexity https://www.perplexity.ai/hub/legal/terms-of-service and https://www.perplexity.ai/hub/legal/privacy-notice; Groq https://groq.com/terms-of-use and https://groq.com/privacy-policy; Cohere https://cohere.com/terms-of-use and https://cohere.com/privacy; Microsoft Azure https://azure.microsoft.com/support/legal and https://privacy.microsoft.com/privacystatement; DeepSeek https://cdn.deepseek.com/policies/en-US/deepseek-terms-of-use.html and https://cdn.deepseek.com/policies/en-US/deepseek-privacy-policy.html; Alibaba Qwen https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/legal and https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/privacy-policy. A self-hosted endpoint sends data only to the server you named.
  • Google Search Console API and Google Analytics Data API (www.googleapis.com, analyticsdata.googleapis.com, analyticsadmin.googleapis.com, oauth2.googleapis.com, accounts.google.com): read-only, to show your search positions and traffic, and only after you connect a Google account — either with “Sign in with Google” (next entry) or with your own Google Cloud OAuth credentials. Sent: your OAuth token and the property you selected, each time the report screens load or the daily snapshot runs. https://policies.google.com/terms and https://policies.google.com/privacy
  • AI Rank Suite connect service (airanksuite.com/google-connect), run by us, the authors of this plugin: used only if you press “Sign in with Google” instead of entering your own Google Cloud credentials. It holds the Google OAuth client, so that you do not have to create a Google Cloud project. Sent when you press the button: your site address, the plugin version and a one-time random value that ties the answer to your browser. Sent afterwards, whenever Google’s access token has expired and a report needs a new one: your site address and the refresh token Google issued for your connection. It receives none of your Search Console or Analytics data. Those requests go from your site to Google directly. Disconnecting, or entering your own credentials, stops all contact.   • Google tag / Google Analytics 4 (www.googletagmanager.com): if you enter a measurement ID, the Google tag is loaded on your public pages and visitors’ page views are reported to Google, subject to the consent banner you configure. https://policies.google.com/terms and https://policies.google.com/privacy
  • Google PageSpeed Insights API (www.googleapis.com): sends a page URL of yours to Google to fetch its performance score, only when you press the button. https://developers.google.com/speed/docs/insights/v5/get-started, https://policies.google.com/terms and https://policies.google.com/privacy

screenshots.caption: The dashboard: your site's AI search score, the three things worth doing next, and the numbers behind them.
